title: Broadway’s latest celebrity-driven play is here and is already breaki...
transcript: If I'm being honest, I've never really cared for waiting for Godot. It is a play where not much happens, and what does happen is quite absurd and quite abstract. On its surface, it is just about two guys who are waiting around for someone who may or may not come. But there is also this deeper layer that is steeped in symbolism and metaphor, although what exactly it's symbolizing is often unclear and something that has been heavily debated since the play came out. And that can sometimes be a frustrating viewing experience when a play is throwing so many questions at you but not providing you any answers. However, as far as productions of got to go, I did really enjoy this one. It is directed by Jamie Lloyd, who has become known for his hyper minimal aesthetic. I think this play is a perfect fit for his sensitivities. He manages to do a lot with a little and keep things moving at a pretty brisk pace and helps avoid a lot of the monotony that I think this play can often fall into. And then, of course, we have to talk about Keanu Reeves and Alex Winter, who are the whole reason that this production even exists. I definitely think Alex Winter is giving the stronger performance of the two. He has one monologue towards the end of the show that I actually thought was really great. I do, however, think that both actors are overshadowed by The two actors playing Pozzo and lucky, they're both giving these really dynamic and exciting performances. That make Alex and Keanu just seem a little bit low energy in comparison. Especially Keanu, I felt, tended to be a little bit one note in his line delivery. And I know that is the type of characters that he is known for playing. But I was hoping to see a little bit more from him here. But I do think, overall, this is a really good production of a play that I just don't really love. I don't think that this is a production that is really going to change anyone's mind on this play. And I do think if you've never seen Godot, this is a decent introduction to it. Just know what you're getting into, because it is a very unique play.
reasoning: Creator praises the production, direction, and supporting cast but is lukewarm on Keanu's performance and admits he doesn't love the play itself. Calls it a 'really good production' but won't change minds — a mixed-to-mildly-positive signal.
